create.name: Iyengar Yoga Centre of Wellington
create.bio:
The Iyengar Yoga Centre of Wellington is a city-centre studio in Te Aro, set upstairs in The Bakehouse, a brick building from 1911 off Cuba Street. Its founding teacher, Tessa Meek, began giving classes in the Aro Valley Community Hall in 1998 and opened the centre at the start of 2007; some of her first students still practise there. She holds a senior Iyengar certificate, has studied with Geeta Iyengar and at the Pune institute, has learned from her own teacher Peter Thomson for some 25 years, and also practises Vipassana meditation.

A small team of certified teachers shares a weekly timetable graded from a four-week beginners' course and Level 1 through to Level 3, with general classes for mixed groups. Some general and Level 2 sessions can be joined by live stream once students know the props. Tessa leads themed Sunday workshops and slower restorative sessions roughly every two months, and runs residential retreats, both in New Zealand, at Wangapeka on the South Island and by Lake Taupō, and overseas in places such as Bali, Bhutan and Sri Lanka, combining posture work with pranayama and meditation.

courses.title: Class memberships and passes
courses.description: Weekly memberships priced per class for one, two or three classes a week, alongside casual drop-ins, a two-month five-class pass, a live-stream pass and a three-class introduction for new students. Passes are bought online or at the studio.
courses.price: $28/class (1 class wk membership); casual $30 per class; New Student Intro 3 classes for $60

courses.title: Weekly classes and workshops (timetable)
courses.description: The online timetable for the centre's graded classes, from Level 1 to Level 3 and general mixed-level sessions, together with Tessa Meek's themed workshops and occasional restorative afternoons. Classes and workshops are booked directly from this page.

courses.title: Wangapeka Retreat
courses.description: A week-long residential retreat at the Wangapeka Retreat Centre in the hills of the South Island, a place the studio returns to often. Days combine posture practice, pranayama and meditation in a quiet rural setting.
